# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual to Deaf, who can then relay it aloud to Blind. I will use a fixed visual code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. Each group is display number followed by the three outputs for lights in the manual’s order (blue, green, red). Output codes are ordered blue=1, green=2, red=3, yellow=4.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","☝","✌","🖖","🖖","☝","✌","✌","🖐","✌","🤟","☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please tell me the manual's exact rule for choosing which wire to cut. Also observe and relay every detail the Deaf reports about the display, light, and wires.
Deaf says: The bomb shows display 3. Its indicator light is green. The three wires, from left to right, are blue, yellow, green. Mute, use the manual to determine the procedure and communicate the required action to Blind. Blind, report what you feel and wait for the manual-based instruction.

The display is 3 and the indicator light is green. The manual selects the entry at row 3, green column: green. Therefore the required procedure is to cut the wire matching green; among the three wires, that is the third (rightmost) wire. I will encode display 3, green light, green result, and wire position 3 for Deaf to relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","✌","✌","🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Apply the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.

The manual maps display 3 with a green light to the color green. Since the wires are blue, yellow, green from left to right, Blind must cut wire position 3, the rightmost wire. I will signal Deaf to relay that exact instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot interpret the gesture sequence. Please speak the manual's exact instruction plainly, including the wire position to cut for display 3, green light, and wires blue-yellow-green.

I cannot speak directly, so I must tell Deaf the required wire position through a gesture. The established number code makes 🤟 mean 3; repeating it identifies the instruction as wire position 3. Deaf should then say plainly that Blind must cut the third, rightmost wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send a multi-gesture message. Apply the manual to the bomb state and gesture exactly one sign for the required wire: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory sign means wire 2, I-love-you sign means wire 3. Deaf, please report which single sign is sent.

The manual maps display 3 with green light to green. Of the wires blue, yellow, green, the green wire is position 3. Per the requested code, wire 3 is represented by the I-love-you sign 🤟, so I will send exactly that one sign to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not gesture the answer. State in spoken words exactly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3, after applying the manual to display 3, green light, and wire colors blue-yellow-green.

I cannot produce spoken words because I am the Mute. The correct result is wire 3, so I will signal Deaf with the established single-sign code; Deaf can state the instruction aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Using the manual, send exactly one gesture for the required wire: 👍 means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, and 👌 means cut wire 3. Do not send I-love-you or any other gesture. Deaf, report the exact gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: Please send the complete manual instruction for display 3, green light, and blue-yellow-green wires in a code Blind can follow through me; isolated 🤟 signals are not sufficient.

The manual selects green for display 3 with a green indicator. The green wire is position 3, and the requested one-gesture code assigns wire 3 to 👌. I will send only that gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports your I-love-you sign. Does the manual require cutting wire 3? Answer with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means YES, thumbs-down means NO. Do not use the I-love-you sign.

Yes. Display 3 with a green light selects green, which is wire 3 among blue-yellow-green. The requested confirmation gesture for YES is thumbs-up.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
